title: Shortest Distance After Road Addition Queries I
summary: Given an integer n and a series of queries, each adding a unidirectional road between two cities.
statement: Given an integer n and a series of queries, each adding a unidirectional road between two cities. After each query, determine the shortest path length from city 0 to city n-1. Return an array where each element represents the shortest path length after processing the first i+1 queries.
constraints: 3≤n≤500; initially every city i has a directed road to i+1.
Each distinct query [u,v] has u+1<v and permanently adds a forward road.
After each addition return the shortest edge count from 0 to n-1.
hints: All roads point forward, so city order is already a topological order.
After each addition, recompute shortest distances by relaxing outgoing roads from left to right.
Start with chain distances 0..n-1; relax every stored edge once and record the last distance.
Topological relaxation considers every possible last edge after its source distance is final, proving the shortest result.
editorial: Topological relaxation considers every possible last edge after its source distance is final, proving the shortest result.

tests.explanation: The new best routes have lengths three, two, then one.
The direct road fixes the distance at one, so the second road cannot improve it.
